s1.quote: The Ozone sits in 3-4M of water, the paddles stick out of the water and it suits snorkeling or scuba diving.

s2.quote: Ozone was withdrawn from service in 1918. In 1925, she was sold for scrap, dismantled and sunk 50m offshore at Indented Head to form a breakwater for small craft. Its wreckage remains visible and is an easy shallow dive.

summary.text: Wreck of a 1886 paddle steamer scuttled as a breakwater off Indented Head in 1925, lying in about 3-4 m so the paddles show. An easy shallow dive or snorkel close to shore.

s1.publisher: Nigel Marsh Photography (Scuba Diver magazine article)
s1.quote: Flinders Reef is the most popular, all weather, dive site on the outer side of Moreton Island … numerous moorings have been placed here to protect the delicate hard corals … the turtles are the main feature at Flinders Reef

highlights.text: Hawksbill and green turtles; cleaning station

s1.publisher: Nigel Marsh Photography (Scuba Diver magazine article)
s1.quote: Henderson Rock and Cherub’s Cave are all similar dive sites … These sites vary in depth from 12m to 30m … it is the grey nurse sharks that make these sites special

s2.quote: off the exposed eastern side of Moreton Island and are generally only dived over the winter months when conditions are calm and grey nurse sharks are in residence

s1.quote: The artificial reef is spread over 400m, in depths from 12m to 30m … the highlight of any dive at Curtin is a close encounter with a giant Queensland groper

Lighthouse Bommie, Lady Elliot Island … Manta Cleaning station, Scenic Reef and mega fauna Depth: Top: 5M Median: 11M Bottom: 16M … Also in the vicinity of the Lighthouse Bommie mooring is a turtle cleaning station

s2.quote: Just off the western side of Lady Elliot Island is a group of small coral outcrops known as Lighthouse Bommies. Descend down the mooring line and drift onto the bommies

mooring.value: Mooring line; descend and drift onto the bommies

summary.text: A group of small bommies off the west side of Lady Elliot Island, reached by a mooring line, famed for manta rays being cleaned by wrasse, with turtles also cleaned nearby.

s1.quote: only one of these can be dived, that is the Severance. This fully intact yacht sank in 1998 … Sitting on a sandy sea floor, 21 metres deep

highlights.text: Intact yacht with soft corals on the rigging

s1.quote: Manta Ray Bommie is not just one coral head, but a collection of bommies off the western side of Lady Musgrave Island … in depths from 12 to 20 metres … the main attraction is the manta rays

highlights.text: Manta rays cleaned atop the bommies

s1.quote: Crystal Palace Skill level: Beginner to intermediate … It’s a reasonably shallow dive, ranging from eight to 18 metres in depth.

s2.quote: Crystal Palace Site Certification Level Located at the southwest end of Rottnest Island, this is a great dive for all levels with a maximum depth of 18m

summary.text: A shallow limestone cave and swim-through site off the south of Rottnest Island, suitable for most divers, with nudibranchs and plenty of fish in the caverns.

s1.quote: Roe Reef is popular due to its easy location, not far from Thompson Bay, and is great for all levels. Swim-throughs at 10–15m; the site is no deeper than 17m.

s2.quote: Roe Reef Skill level: All levels … The reef itself is a series of small caves around 14m in depth, where you’ll find tight swim-throughs and a giant limestone arch

summary.text: An easy Rottnest Island reef of small caves around 14 m with tight swim-throughs and a large limestone arch, good for all levels when swell is low.

s1.quote: Opera House itself is a rock inside the larger cave system, up to 31 metres in depth. Rays of light illuminate the caverns

s2.quote: Opera House is a grand diving spot, a spectacular concourse of caves galore. The deep dive (30 metres) offers the most impressive light show underwater

highlights.text: Caverns lit by shafts of light

summary.text: A deep cave system on a limestone slope off Rottnest, with light shafts through the caverns, overhangs and occasional grey nurse sharks, reaching around 30 m.

s1.quote: Shark Cave (Cathedral Rocks) Skill level: Advanced … descending to 26 metres at the back of the cave … the strong surface currents can be a challenge

s2.quote: Shark Cave – also known as Nurse’s Quarters – is a haven for endangered grey nurse sharks … Please note: Shark Cave is suited to advanced divers only.

highlights.text: Grey nurse sharks resting in the cave

s2.quote: A 35-minute drive southwest from Perth is Ammo Jetty … the maximum depth is usually between 23 to 30 feet (7 to 9 m)

s1.quote: The Cod Hole This dive site consists of two bommies submersed in 18m of water, joined together by a natural arch. One bommie rises up to 10m, the other to 6m.

s1.quote: EX-HMAS SWAN Dunsborough, Western Australia Type of dive: Scuttled warship … Scuba: Advanced (Supervised Open Water) Access: Boat only (20 minutes) Depth: 9 – 30 metres

s2.quote: HMAS Swan Dive Wreck is about a 15-minute boat ride out to sea from Meelup Beach … dive the Swan from a private boat by obtaining an access permit from the Dunsborough Visitor Centre

s3.quote: Ex-HMAS Swan now sits upright on her keel in 30 metres (100’) of water … Large schools of bullseyes inhabit the inner spaces

s4.quote: The 113-metre-long decommissioned naval destroyer was scuttled in Geographe Bay off Dunsborough in 1997 … Sitting in 35 metres of water and with a slight list

access.value: Boat only; private boats need a permit from Dunsborough Visitor Centre

highlights.text: Schools of bullseyes inside the hull

summary.text: Former navy destroyer scuttled in 1997 off Dunsborough, upright in roughly 30-35 m with parts of the superstructure intact and bullseyes filling the rooms.
